S1.why: Adjective alone in feminine-plural form agreeing with the implied cutling-uri; the tiles above are the noun.

S2.why: An invitation in the informal tu the vocabulary uses; reads as carrying on, not as a limit.

S3.s: Ai folosit toate cele %lld cutling-uri gratuite. Rămân gratuite și merg ca până acum.
S3.back: You-have used all the 5 cutlings free. Stay-they free and work-they as until now.
S3.why: Lowercase cutling-uri mid-sentence as in the vocabulary's sentence; „merg ca până acum” is how a Romanian says things keep working unchanged.

S4.why: States the fact instead of „you can”; no „de” because 5 takes the noun directly.

S5.s: Ai folosit %lld din cele %lld cutling-uri gratuite.
S5.back: You-have used 3 of the 5 cutlings free.
S5.why: Numbers keep the brief's order, so no positional forms; „din cele” is the natural partitive.

S6.why: Numbers 20 and up take „de” before the noun, and 5.000 always does; the grey line under it says what fills that room.

S7.s: Până la %@ de texte și %lld de imagini.
S7.back: Up to 5.000 of texts and 500 of images.
S7.why: „Text” and „Imagini” from the vocabulary; both counts take „de” as Romanian requires for 500 and 5.000.

S8.why: Romanian lists three with „și” and no comma before it.

S9.s: Achiziția e valabilă pe orice dispozitiv conectat la contul tău Apple.
S9.back: The-purchase is valid on any device connected to the-account your Apple.
S9.why: Reuses the vocabulary's „dispozitiv conectat la contul Apple”; „valabilă” is what Romanians say of a purchase or ticket that covers something.

S10.why: Short noun phrase for the bold line; „plată unică” sounds like an invoice, this sounds like a person.

S11.s: Fără abonament, fără reclame, fără înregistrare.
S11.back: Without subscription, without ads, without registration.
S11.why: „Înregistrare” is the everyday word for signing up; the repeated „fără” is how the phrase is said aloud.

S12.why: The wording Romanian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action, in tu imperative.

S13.why: Impersonal reflexive for a process under way, with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: Tu imperative like the vocabulary's „Activează”; „pentru” + price is how a Romanian button states a cost.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price.

S16.why: What a Romanian says to put something off politely, without refusing.

S17.why: The label Romanian iOS gives its close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and a little proud; „e” is the spoken form of „este”.

S19.s: Mulțumesc. Cutling e făcut de un singur om, iar tu tocmai l-ai ajutat.
S19.back: Thank-I. Cutling is made by one single man, and you just him-have helped.
S19.why: First person singular because one person makes the app; the thanks is tied to a fact instead of a slogan.

S20.s: Bine ai revenit. Achiziția ta e din nou activă.
S20.back: Well you-have returned. The-purchase your is again active.
S20.why: „Bine ai revenit” is the standard warm greeting for a returning user; „achiziția” matches S9.

S21.why: Spoken form of S5; works for any first number because the verb does not agree with it.

S22.s: Cutling-uri salvate: %lld. Acum ai loc pentru %@.
S22.back: Cutlings saved: 5. Now you-have room for 5.000.
S22.why: Count after a label so 1, 2, 5 and 21 all read correctly (21 would otherwise need „de”); 5.000 ends the sentence, so no „de” either.

S23.s: Cutling e deblocat. Ai loc pentru %@ de cutling-uri.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. You-have room for 5.000 of cutlings.
S23.why: Masculine-neuter „deblocat” for the app's name; „de” after 5.000.

S24.why: The calm phrase Romanian shops use for an unfinished order; no subject to blame.

S25.s: App Store nu răspunde momentan. Încearcă din nou puțin mai târziu.
S25.back: App Store not responds at-the-moment. Try again a-little more late.
S25.why: „Nu răspunde” instead of a passive „nu poate fi accesat”, which reads translated.

S26.s: App Store nu a confirmat achiziția.
S26.back: App Store not has confirmed the-purchase.
S26.why: One plain sentence; the OK button is the way out.

S27.s: Contul Apple de pe acest dispozitiv nu are nicio achiziție Cutling anterioară.
S27.back: The-account Apple from on this device not has no purchase Cutling earlier.
S27.why: Romanian double negative „nu … nicio”; „dispozitiv” and „contul Apple” from the vocabulary.

S28.s: Versiunea gratuită păstrează %lld cutling-uri. Deblochează Cutling o dată și salvezi câte vrei.
S28.back: The-version free keeps 5 cutlings. Unlock Cutling one time and save-you how-many want-you.
S28.why: „Câte vrei” is the spoken way to say as many as you like; imperative then present is how Romanian states a consequence.

S29.why: Sits under the „Cutling-uri” title, which supplies the noun; fits the 18-character budget.

K1.why: „Gratis” is the spoken word and fits the 38-character capsule where „gratuite” would not; the verb tells the person what tapping does.

M1.why: Verb-led command name, as Romanian Mac window titles are.

M2.why: Same command as M1 with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Capitalised „Cutling-uri” as in the vocabulary's list title, since it starts the row label.

M4.why: „din” is the compact Romanian number pair; a slash reads technical.

M5.why: Same phrase as S23 so the state has one name.

M6.s: O singură achiziție deblochează Cutling pe iPhone, iPad și Mac.
M6.back: A single purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: „Achiziție” as in S9 and S24; device list as in S8.

M7.s: Deblocat pe iPhone, iPad și Mac cu acest cont Apple.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this account Apple.
M7.why: „cont Apple” from the vocabulary; participle agrees with Cutling, the section's name.

M8.s: Ai cumpărat Cutling înainte să devină gratuit, așa că rămâne deblocat. Mulțumesc.
M8.back: You-have bought Cutling before to become-it free, so that stays-it unlocked. Thank-I.
M8.why: „Așa că” is the spoken because-so; the thanks is first person singular like S19.
